sections.title: Model overview and intended purpose
sections.text: Python Random Forest (model_id python-random-forest) is a scikit-learn classifier that predicts the binary target default.payment.next.month on the UCI Default of Credit Card Clients dataset (30,000 records of credit-card clients in Taiwan, April to September 2005). Its stated business purpose is a benchmark model for internal analysis that is not used in decisions, but this purpose was inferred rather than documented. The business owner and intended business use are not documented. The model is recorded as risk tier 3.

sections.title: Algorithm and methodology
sections.text: The model is a scikit-learn RandomForestClassifier with 150 trees, random_state set by a seed (default 42), n_jobs=-1 and class_weight="balanced" to handle class imbalance, using 21 inferred input features: LIMIT_BAL, EDUCATION, MARRIAGE, PAY_0 and PAY_2 to PAY_6, BILL_AMT1 to BILL_AMT6, and PAY_AMT1 to PAY_AMT6. Preprocessing drops ID, handles missing values by loader (the Excel loader drops rows with missing values, while the official loader rejects them during a validation step that checks 30,000 rows, 25 columns and a 20-24% default rate), casts the target to int, and applies no scaling or encoding. SEX and AGE are excluded as predictors and are intended only for fairness analysis. Data are split with a stratified 80/20 train/test split (random_state=42), and a 0.5 decision threshold is recorded; the train fraction and threshold are both inferred values.

sections.title: Limitations and assumptions
sections.text: No validation metrics, fairness results or prediction PSI are recorded, and performance acceptance criteria, the threshold actually used in validation and monitoring, the rationale for the hyperparameters, and approval, version and deployment details are not documented. Labels are not produced at the legacy model's 0.35 threshold, so they may not be comparable with the migration candidate's labels. The model_identity hash covers only the feature list for this model, because the random forest has no param_names, and a demo fixture with a reduced, synthetic feature set may be used when the UCI data are unavailable. The dataset is public demonstration data that is not representative of a UK bank's current portfolio, and the data time period and representativeness are listed as missing information.
